newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai finance ministry plans fund to help bourse.
newsitem.headline: Thai finance ministry plans fund to help bourse.

text.p: Thailand's finance ministry plans to set up a 10-billion-baht fund to be used to buy stocks that might be force-sold by brokerages on the depressed stockmarket, a senior ministry official said on Wednesday.
The ministry's permanent secretary Chatu Mongkul Sonakul told reporters the Government Savings Bank would be assigned to raise the funds.
Further details on how and when the fund would operate would be worked out by ministry officials later this week.
The fund was expected to be available next week, the ministry official said without elaborating.
Chatu Mongkul said the current level of the rumour-hit bourse, where the stock index has plummeted to near three-year lows, did not reflect the real demand and supply situation in the market.

He added that the fund was not aimed at pushing up prices but rather to limit forced selling on the market of stocks held by financially-weak investors unable to top up margin calls requested by brokerages.
The forced selling of stocks, after rumours from last Friday that some brokerages had been hit by client defaults on margin loans, had depressed the Thai bourse.

The stock market finished up on Wednesday, breaking nine consecutive days of falls, as an undisclosd sum of money from another 15.7 billion baht rescue fund set up by bankers amd brokers, entered the market to shore up prices, brokers said.
The index ended up 1.44 percent or 14.13 points at 996.16.
